recipes.name: Hominy corn porridge
steps: Soak dried hominy overnight in plenty of water.
Drain and simmer in fresh water until the kernels are tender, often 1–2 hours.
Add coconut milk and cinnamon and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Stir in nutmeg and sugar; thin with water if needed, and serve warm.

recipes.name: Green banana porridge
steps: Peel green bananas with a knife and wash off sap.
Blend chopped banana with 250 ml water to a smooth paste.
Bring remaining water to a simmer and whisk in banana mixture gradually.
Cook stirring 12–18 minutes until cooked through and thickened; add coconut milk and spices.
Simmer 5 minutes and sweeten to taste.

recipes.name: Plantain porridge
steps: Peel and chop plantains; blend with 250 ml water until smooth.
Simmer remaining water with cinnamon.
Whisk in blended plantain and cook, stirring frequently, for 12–15 minutes.
Add coconut milk and nutmeg; cook until no raw starchy flavor remains.
Sweeten and serve hot.

recipes.name: Peanut porridge
steps: Blend peanuts, oats and 300 ml water until smooth.
Bring remaining water to a simmer and whisk in the mixture.
Cook over low heat 12–15 minutes, stirring to prevent sticking.
Add milk, cinnamon and sugar and simmer another 5 minutes.
Serve hot; identify peanut allergens clearly.

recipes.name: Oats porridge
steps: Combine oats and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring for 5–8 minutes until oats soften.
Add milk, cinnamon and nutmeg; cook another 3–5 minutes.
Sweeten to taste and adjust thickness with additional water.
Serve warm.

recipes.name: Stamp and go
steps: Simmer salted cod in fresh water, repeat as needed, remove bones and flake.
Combine flour, baking powder and water to form a thick batter.
Mix in cod, finely chopped onion, scallion and pepper.
Heat shallow oil over medium heat, drop spoonfuls and fry on both sides until browned and cooked through.
Drain and serve hot.

recipes.name: Callaloo omelette
steps: Whisk eggs with black pepper.
Squeeze extra moisture from cooked callaloo and chop finely.
Sauté chopped scallion and tomato in oil for 2 minutes, then add callaloo.
Pour in eggs and cook over low heat until just set, folding once.
Serve immediately; cook eggs thoroughly for vulnerable diners.

recipes.name: Steamed cabbage breakfast
steps: Wash and finely slice cabbage and other vegetables.
Soften onion and sweet pepper in oil for 3 minutes.
Add carrot, cabbage, scallion, thyme and water.
Cover and steam 8–12 minutes until vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Remove lid to reduce liquid and season to taste.

recipes.name: Boiled green banana
steps: Trim ends and score skin lengthwise without cutting deep into the flesh.
Cover green bananas with water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer 15–25 minutes, depending on size, until easily pierced.
Cool enough to handle, remove skins and serve with saltfish or vegetables.
Use care when peeling hot bananas.

recipes.name: Boiled yam and dumpling
steps: Peel yam thickly with a knife, wash and cut into pieces; some yams irritate skin.
Mix flour, salt and enough water into a firm dough; shape small dumplings.
Bring water to a full boil and add yam pieces.
After 5 minutes add dumplings and simmer 15–20 minutes until yam and dumplings are fully cooked.
Drain and serve warm.

recipes.name: Pumpkin rice
steps: Peel pumpkin and cut into small cubes.
Sauté chopped onion and scallion in oil for 3 minutes.
Add pumpkin, water and thyme; simmer 8 minutes until pumpkin softens.
Add rinsed rice and stir once, then cover and cook low 18–22 minutes until rice is tender.
Rest 10 minutes and fluff.

recipes.name: Curried shrimp
steps: Pat shrimp dry and toss with half the curry powder.
Heat oil, gently cook remaining curry powder 20 seconds, then soften onion and pepper.
Add garlic and coconut milk; simmer 4 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 3–5 minutes, stirring, until opaque and firm.
Serve promptly over rice.

recipes.name: Stewed lentils
steps: Rinse lentils and check for small stones.
Sauté onion, scallion, carrot and garlic in a little water or oil.
Add lentils, thyme and water; simmer 20–30 minutes until tender.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer 5–10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Season and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Coconut shrimp
steps: Dry shrimp and refrigerate until ready to cook.
Sauté onion and bell pepper in oil for 4 minutes; add garlic and thyme.
Add coconut milk and simmer 5–7 minutes to concentrate the sauce.
Add shrimp and cook until opaque and firm, typically 3–5 minutes.
Taste sauce and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Fried sprat
steps: Clean fish appropriately and pat dry; keep chilled.
Season with lime, salt and pepper, then coat lightly in flour.
Heat a shallow layer of oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry in batches until crisp and cooked through, turning carefully.
Drain on a rack; small fish may contain fine bones.

recipes.name: Cornmeal pudding
steps: Heat oven to 175°C/350°F and grease a baking dish.
Whisk cornmeal into half the cool water to prevent lumps.
Heat coconut milk, remaining water, sugar and spices until warm; whisk in cornmeal slurry.
Stir over low heat until just thickening, then pour into the dish and add raisins if using.
Bake about 50–70 minutes until firm in the center; cool before slicing.

recipes.name: Coconut drops
steps: Line a tray with baking parchment.
Bring sugar and water to a gentle boil in a heavy pot.
Add diced coconut, ginger and salt, stirring to prevent burning.
Cook until syrup thickens and clings to coconut; drop spoonfuls onto prepared tray.
Cool completely before handling; hot sugar causes burns.

recipes.name: Tamarind balls
ingredients: 150 g brown sugar plus extra for rolling
steps: Check tamarind pulp carefully for hard seeds and shell fragments.
Knead pulp with brown sugar, adding enough to make a cohesive, tangy paste.
Divide into small portions and roll into balls with clean hands.
Roll in extra sugar and leave briefly to firm.
Store covered and refrigerate if keeping beyond the day.

recipes.name: Soursop juice
ingredients: 250 ml milk or coconut milk optional
steps: Wash and peel soursop; separate flesh from peel.
Remove every hard black seed and discard; never blend seeds.
Blend seed-free pulp with water until smooth.
Strain if preferred; stir in milk, nutmeg and sugar to taste.
Refrigerate promptly and serve cold.

recipes.name: Mint tea
steps: Wash mint leaves carefully.
Bring water to a boil and remove from heat.
Add mint leaves, cover and steep 5–8 minutes.
Strain into cups and sweeten if desired.
Serve warm.
